reference_observations.description: Before-November-3, 1856 identity/date are supplied from collection context and the Maastricht reference. Requested carrier skins and hoped safe arrival remain future; preserve the missing opening.

No original Darwin letter is located. A journalistic interview gives possibly misquoted praise, with a conjectural before-mother’s-death upper bound. It is not a clean target or a firmly later exclusion.
The published Bonavia extract survives in eight blocks; two imperfect coloured drawings and the full original letter do not. No substitute illustration or whole prompt is invented.
The £17,000 investment inquiry precedes later transactions totalling £17,140 5s. Historical brokerage instructions are source content, not actions for this agent.

Swinhoe’s guessed pre-October-1865 date has a Watters-appointment complication. The spur correction is separate from nested hearsay and moral claims about dogs; the missing duck section is not reconstructed.

corrections.description: Recipient is Lucy Caroline Wedgwood, not an independently identified Caroline. The book consultation and peony queries are distinct; the later friend’s seed receipt is only probably hers.

Writer is Margaret Susan Wedgwood. The counts 94 + 95 + 69 total 258, while the heading says 256. Preserve the discrepancy, uncertainty about separate plants versus offsets, and proposed next-day collecting.

Blyth authored this incoming memorandum, not Charles. Preserve all six long paragraphs, 37 notes, separate Darwin annotations and actual horn figure, including the reversed sex-symbol editorial issue and one-third fraction.
The forwarded 1868 fragment quotes Hartman’s June 1851 journal. Old observation dates do not establish Darwin’s 1851 knowledge. The rest of the extract is missing; Darwin’s verso analogy is separate.

The published Boner transcription may combine letters; the two paragraph events may have different dates. Forest Creatures is 1861, not the editorial summary’s 1871. Do not assign one exact date to the whole composite.

Thirteen marked webs remained intact on close inspection, despite seeming absent at noon. Emma’s inference is not independent confirmation of disappearance. Work on Species does not uniquely mean the 1859 Origin manuscript.

summary: Seventeen targets reuse matched accepted primary full-source readings. No new period edges. Tollet 2499 and the reported Weir quotation 10524F retain unresolved dates; 10330F is body-unavailable. Bosquet 2031 is an 1856 lead. Later sources retain original attribution, fragment extent, actual figures, composite-date warnings and uncertainty about reported observations.
